title: Riesz-energy initial configuration
spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres of a fraction (say half) of non-guided restarts with a configuration obtained by minimising the Riesz energy sum over pairs of 1/||c_i - c_j||^s plus a wall term that keeps centres in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Draw the exponent s uniformly from [1, 8] using the seed rng, run 100 L-BFGS-B iterations with numeric or analytic gradient from a random start, then pass the result to the existing SLSQP stage with initial radius INIT_RADIUS. This gives well-spread starts without any explicit circle layout.

title: Stretched-box warm start
spec: For a restart, pick a random aspect ratio a from [0.85, 1.15]. Solve the SLSQP packing in the rectangle [0, a] x [0, 1] with its own wall constraints, starting from a uniform random layout, with a and the walls as fixed parameters. Then rescale the centres to x times 1/a so that they fit the unit square. Use the rescaled centres as the start for a second SLSQP solve in the unit square, with the usual INIT_RADIUS. This gives structured starts from different geometries while keeping every initial state inside the square.

title: Size-class homotopy with k discrete radius classes
spec: For a fraction of restarts, assign each circle to one of k = 3 size classes, with k drawn from {2, 3} and class sizes set by a seeded random split of n. Solve SLSQP in which circles in the same class share a common radius variable, so the radius vector has k entries. This is a small, low-dimensional problem and converges quickly. Then release the class constraints by giving each circle its own radius, starting from the class radii, and run a final SLSQP solve with the usual constraints. Repair and keep the best result. This is a size-class homotopy and it is not the single equal-radius stage already tried.

title: Cyclic relocation sweep on the incumbent
spec: After repair, run a local search on the best packing. Pick a random circle, remove it, and find the point in the square that allows the largest radius for it given the other circles, using a grid search over candidate points followed by a local Nelder-Mead refinement, which makes the candidate radius equal to the minimum of the clearance to the walls and to the other circles. If the new total sum of radii, after re-optimising the other radii with a short SLSQP on fixed centres, is higher than the old sum, keep the move. Repeat for about 40 random circles or until the time slice runs out. This is a deterministic, hole-targeted move that differs from random jitter.

title: Divide-and-conquer quadrant packing
spec: For about a third of the non-guided restarts, split n into four groups of roughly n/4 (by random assignment from the seeded rng). Solve each group independently as a packing in its own quadrant of the unit square (quadrant side 0.5 with the same SLSQP model), then rescale the four solutions into the full square with their centres and radii halved. Feed the merged packing to one global SLSQP stage as the start, then repair as usual. This tests whether recursive structure helps the search reach the good configurations.

title: Over-inflated overlapping starts
spec: For a random half of the non-guided restarts, set the initial radii to 0.12 instead of INIT_RADIUS=0.05, keeping the uniform random centres. SLSQP starts with heavy overlaps and must resolve them, which may land in different basins than the usual feasible-ish start. Keep the rest of the pipeline (clip, repair, best-of selection) unchanged. The seed rng decides which restarts are inflated.

title: Relocate the smallest circle into the largest hole
spec: After each repair in the restart loop, take the incumbent (or the current candidate) and remove the circle with the smallest radius. Find the largest empty region by sampling about 2000 seeded random points and taking the one with the greatest distance to all remaining centres and walls. Place the removed circle there with radius 0, then run one SLSQP solve from that start with MAX_ITER and the usual constraints. Keep the result only if its repaired sum of radii beats the incumbent. This is a single, self-contained move, separate from the zero-contact rattler reinsertion idea.

title: Concentric-ring initialisation near the walls
spec: For a random subset of non-guided restarts, seed the centres on concentric rings. Choose a random number of rings k in {2, 3}. Place the rings at distances from the walls that are spaced evenly, with the outer ring just inside the square. Distribute the n circles across the rings in proportion to each ring's circumference, with a seeded random phase and a small jitter. Set the initial radii to INIT_RADIUS and run the normal SLSQP. This mimics the ring-like structure that large packings often show near the boundary, and it is distinct from the hexagonal and symmetric seeds already tried.

title: Power-diagram Lloyd relaxation between SLSQP solves
spec: After each repaired SLSQP restart, run 5 weighted Lloyd iterations on the centres. Assign every sample point in a fine grid (about 200x200) to the circle with the smallest power distance |p - c_i|^2 - r_i^2, then move each centre to the centroid of its power cell. Keep the radii fixed during this step. Then repair and pass the result to a second short SLSQP run with 100 iterations. Keep whichever of the two results has the larger sum of radii. Use only numpy, and draw any randomness from the seed rng.

title: Heavy-tailed Levy jumps of single circles
spec: Replace the guided restart's centre jitter with a Levy-type jump. Pick 1 to 3 random circles, weighted toward the smallest radii, and move each to a new position drawn uniformly over the square. The jump length is heavy-tailed: each jump is the uniform position with probability 0.5, otherwise a step of length 0.5 * U^(-1/1.5) in a random direction, clipped to the square. Assign the moved circles the minimum radius of the incumbent. Then run the existing SLSQP and repair steps. The rest of the restart logic is unchanged.

title: Vacancy-defect hexagonal starts
spec: For a random subset of the non-guided restarts, build a hexagonal lattice whose site count is about n+k, with k drawn uniformly from 2 to 6. Remove k random sites so that the lattice has n points, then add Gaussian jitter of scale 0.02 and clip to [0.05, 0.95]. Choose the lattice orientation, the spacing and the offset at random from the seed rng. Pass these centres to the existing SLSQP call with the usual initial radius. Keep the rest of the restart logic unchanged.

title: Contact-gap pull regularizer annealed to zero
spec: Add a term mu * sum over pairs of max(0, d_ij - r_i - r_j)^2 to the SLSQP objective, with a pull toward contact, where mu starts at 0.05 in the first SLSQP call of each restart and decays geometrically to 0 across the restart's time slice. The final SLSQP call uses mu=0 so the constraints are exact. The term encourages rigid, touching structures before the free radii are optimised. Use the existing pair-based constraint set and the repair step unchanged.

title: Ruin-and-recreate on k random small circles
spec: After the random-restart loop, take the incumbent and pick k uniformly from {2,...,5} from rng. Remove the k circles with the smallest radii and reinsert each one at the point, out of 3000 uniform random candidates in [0,1]^2, that maximises the distance to all remaining centres minus their radii (the largest free space). Set the reinserted radii to 0.01, then run SLSQP from this start and keep the result if its repaired sum of radii is larger. Repeat for as long as the time budget allows. This moves whole sets of small circles, not one at a time.

title: Outer-shell first, then interior insertion
spec: For half of the non-guided restarts, solve in two stages. First place a shell of 20 circles on a rectangle inset by a random margin in [0.05, 0.15] around the boundary, using random positions along its edges. Run SLSQP on those 20 circles alone with the 12 remaining circles absent. Then add the 12 interior circles at random positions in the interior, and run a full SLSQP on all 32. The shell fixes the boundary structure, and the interior pass fills the gaps. Repair as usual.

title: Weighted-scale pre-stage with fixed relative radii
spec: Before the free-radius SLSQP stage, draw positive fixed weights w_i uniformly from [0.6, 1.4] per restart from rng. Solve a problem with variables (centres, scale s): maximise s subject to the pair and boundary constraints, with radii r_i = s * w_i. Use SLSQP with the same constraint form as now. Then use the centres and radii r_i = s * w_i as the start for the existing free-radius stage. This gives the optimiser a non-uniform size mix that is different from the equal-radius and random starts already tried.

title: Contact-cluster displacement kick
spec: After the random-restart loop, build the contact graph of the best packing, where two circles are in contact if the gap is below 1e-6. Pick a random contact cluster of 3 to 6 connected circles using the seed rng. Translate the cluster as a block by a random vector of length 0.05 to 0.15. Clip, repair, and run SLSQP for 100 iterations. Accept the result only if its sum of radii is larger than the incumbent's. Repeat for up to 25 kicks or until the time runs out. This moves whole rigid groups instead of single circles.

title: Radius-cap homotopy in the initial solve
spec: For each non-guided restart, start with a common upper bound R_cap on all radii, set to 0.12 at the start and 0.5 at the end. Solve SLSQP with the constraint r_i <= R_cap at three values of the cap, 0.12, 0.2, and 0.5, warm-starting each solve from the previous one. Then solve once more with no cap and the usual constraints. The cap stops early circles from absorbing all of the free space, so the packing spreads out before the final free-radius solve. Repair as usual.

title: Reflection-symmetric reduced-variable stage
spec: For a random subset of restarts (for example 30 percent), impose mirror symmetry about the vertical line x = 0.5. Use m = n//2 free centres and their mirror images, plus one centre on the axis when n is odd. Build the full centre array from the free variables and the radii as free variables, and run SLSQP on this reduced vector with the same constraints evaluated on the full set. Then unfold, run one unconstrained SLSQP polish on all 2n+n variables, and repair. This is distinct from the existing central-symmetry stage, because it uses a reflection instead of a point reflection.

title: Jitter-scale ladder cohorts around the incumbent
spec: Organise the guided restarts into cohorts of 4. For each cohort, draw a jitter amplitude from the log-uniform set {0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.2} using the seed rng, then start all 4 members of the cohort from the incumbent centres plus Gaussian noise of that amplitude. The cohort winner becomes a candidate for the incumbent. Small amplitudes do local polishing and large ones explore new basins. Keep the 50/50 guided and non-guided split and the 80 percent time fraction unchanged.

title: Mixed restart cadence by cohort
spec: Divide the budget into cohorts of 40 restarts. Within each cohort, alternate the start type: odd restarts use uniform random centres, even restarts use the incumbent with jitter sd drawn log-uniformly from [0.005, 0.1] for that restart. Each cohort starts from the current incumbent, not from the cohort's best. Keep the same SLSQP call and repair. This changes only the schedule of the start-type mix and the jitter scale, so it tests whether a varied jitter scale helps where a fixed one has not.

title: Clustered start from k random cluster centres
spec: For a fraction of random restarts, pick k = 3 or 4 cluster centres uniformly from [0.2, 0.8]^2 using rng. Assign each circle to a cluster at random, then place it at a Gaussian offset of sd 0.12 from its cluster centre, clipped to [0.05, 0.95]. Use these centres as the start for the usual SLSQP call, with the initial radius unchanged. This produces starts with a multi-cluster density structure, which random uniform starts rarely give, and it stays within the existing solve pipeline.

title: Shrink-then-regrow radius homotopy
spec: For each restart, after the first SLSQP solve, multiply all radii by a factor 0.9 with centres fixed and re-solve SLSQP with the radii as variables starting from these shrunken values. Then repeat the shrink-and-solve step once more with factor 0.97. The homotopy moves the optimiser through a sequence of slightly feasible states and lets circles reorganise before the final free-radius solve. Repair and selection are unchanged. This is a schedule over the solve, not an initialisation.

title: Lazy pairwise constraint generation
spec: Inside _solve_once, first run SLSQP with only the non-overlap constraints for pairs whose start centres are within 2.5 times the start radius sum, plus all wall constraints. After each solve, compute all pairwise violations of the returned packing. If any pair with distance less than r_i + r_j minus 1e-6 is missing from the set, add those pairs and re-solve from the last iterate. Stop after 5 rounds or when none are violated. This is exact at convergence, unlike a fixed pair subset, which failed earlier because it used the starting centres only.

title: Spectral low-mode perturbation of the incumbent
spec: Build the contact graph of the incumbent packing, joining circles whose gap is below 1e-3, and compute the eigenvectors of its graph Laplacian. For each guided restart, choose a random low-frequency eigenvector (among the 2nd to 6th smallest eigenvalues) and a random sign, and displace each centre along that vector by an amount 0.05 times the vector entry, separately for x and y coordinates. Start SLSQP from these displaced centres with the incumbent radii. This moves the packing along its collective vibration modes instead of uniformly at random.

title: Repulsive random-field early stage
spec: For each non-guided restart, add a temporary repulsive potential to the SLSQP objective during its first 30 iterations. The potential is sum_i exp(-|c_i - q|^2 / 0.05) for a random point q drawn from the seed rng in [0,1]^2, weighted by a coefficient of 0.02. Remove the term for the remaining iterations, so the final solve optimises the true sum of radii. The point q pushes circles away from one region and so breaks symmetric initial configurations. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

title: Half-plane cut-and-splice crossover of elite packings
spec: Keep the top 4 distinct repaired packings from the random-restart loop. For each guided restart, pick two parents at random from the elite, draw a random line through the unit square (random normal direction, offset uniform in [0.3, 0.7]), take the circles of parent A lying on one side of the line and the circles of parent B on the other side, and fix the count to n by dropping the smallest-radius surplus circles or adding random centres for any deficit. Run the existing jitter, SLSQP and repair pipeline on the spliced centres. This is a geometric crossover, not the index-wise crossover tried before, and it uses only the seeded rng.

title: Affine shear kick of the incumbent
spec: For guided restarts, instead of adding isotropic noise to the incumbent centres, apply a random area-preserving affine map to them. Draw a 2x2 matrix A = I + s * G, where G has independent standard normal entries and s is 0.04, then re-centre about (0.5, 0.5) and rescale the result so that all centres lie in [0.05, 0.95]. Start SLSQP from the transformed centres with the incumbent radii scaled by 0.95. This explores sheared variants of the best basin, which rotations and isotropic jitter do not reach.

title: Radius-weighted restart budget
spec: Keep the same random-restart loop, but give each candidate a weight based on its repaired sum of radii relative to the incumbent. After each restart, record the repaired sum s. Compute the weight w = exp((s - best_sum) / T), with T set to 0.01 and best_sum the current incumbent sum. Use these weights to choose the parent of each guided restart by a categorical draw from the stored repaired packings, instead of always using the single best. Keep at most 30 stored packings and drop the lowest-weight ones. Guidance is still used with the same probability as before, so only the choice of parent changes.

title: Soft-min clearance continuation with log-sum-exp
spec: Add a continuation on the constraint form in SLSQP. In the first stage, replace the hard pairwise and wall constraints with one smooth objective: maximise sum of radii minus (1/beta) times log-sum-exp over all clearances, where clearance is distance minus radius sum for pairs and wall distance minus radius for walls. Use beta = 20, then 80, then 320, each solved with L-BFGS-B using analytic gradients. Finish with the existing SLSQP hard-constraint solve from the result. Beta raises the sharpness of the clearance minimum, so the interior of the feasible set is explored before the constraints become hard.

title: Position-swap kick between unequal circles
spec: For guided restarts, take the incumbent packing and pick two circles i and j whose radii differ by at least 30 percent. Swap their centres (not their radii), so each large circle moves to a small circle's place and the reverse. Then run the usual SLSQP solve from the swapped configuration with a small Gaussian jitter of 0.01 on the centres. This is a discrete move that jumps between basins which a continuous jitter rarely reaches. Apply it to a random 50 percent of guided restarts and keep the rest of the guidance logic unchanged.

title: Three-level schedule that spends the last 20 percent on one long SLSQP
spec: Keep the random restarts for the first 60 percent of the time fraction. In the next 25 percent, run guided restarts from the incumbent with jitter amplitude that halves every 10 restarts. For the final 15 percent, take the top 3 distinct repaired packings and run one _solve_once from each with MAX_ITER raised to 1000 and zero jitter, then repair. The incumbent is the best repaired result. The only change is the time split and the final long solve; the restart logic is otherwise unchanged.

title: Annulus-preserving core rotation kick
spec: After the random-restart loop, generate up to 20 perturbed packings from the best one. For each, choose the circles whose centres lie within radius 0.3 of (0.5, 0.5) as the core. Rotate their centres about (0.5, 0.5) by a random angle drawn from the seed rng in [-0.5, 0.5] radians, and leave the outer ring fixed. Clip and repair, then run SLSQP with 100 iterations. Keep the packing with the largest sum of radii. This kicks the interior arrangement while the walls stay in contact with the boundary circles.

title: Contact-rewiring kick of the incumbent
spec: In the guided branch, take the incumbent and find the pairs whose gap is below 1e-6 after repair (the contact graph). Pick one contact pair at random from rng. For that restart, drop only that pair's constraint in the SLSQP call and keep all others. Solve, repair, and keep the packing only if it beats the incumbent. The step tests whether a single contact can be released to open a different structure, and it differs from the random-subset and lazy-constraint variants already listed.

title: UCB bandit over restart modes
spec: Replace the fixed guided probability in solve with an upper-confidence-bound bandit over two arms, a fresh random start and a guided start from the incumbent. For each arm, track the number of pulls and the mean improvement in the sum of radii over the incumbent, where improvement is zero when the restart does not beat the incumbent. At each restart, choose the arm with the highest mean plus sqrt(2 ln(T) / pulls), with a constraint that each arm is pulled at least twice first. This replaces the time-based switch at half budget, so guidance starts as soon as it proves useful and stops if it does not. Use the seed argument for all randomness.

title: Stochastic boundary-contact relaxation of the incumbent
spec: At the start of each guided restart, apply a short stochastic relaxation to the incumbent before SLSQP. For 200 steps, pick a random circle, move its centre by a Gaussian with sd 0.01 scaled by its radius, and accept the move if no pairwise overlap or wall violation is created when the radius is kept equal to the current value. If rejected, keep the old position. Then run the usual SLSQP from the relaxed centres. This is a Monte Carlo move that can slide circles past each other to escape jammed configurations, and it is a different perturbation type from Gaussian jitter of all centres.

title: Decaying jitter amplitude for guided restarts
spec: In guided restarts, the global jitter of the incumbent centres currently uses a fixed normal scale of 0.03. Replace it with a scale that decays geometrically with the fraction of the guided phase elapsed, from 0.08 at its start to 0.005 at the end of the time budget. Apply the same decay to the radii: start them at 0.9 times the incumbent radii and let SLSQP recover the rest. Keep the choice of guided versus random restarts as it is now.

title: Random-key genetic algorithm over greedy insertion order
spec: Encode a packing as a random-key vector of length n whose argsort gives the insertion order. Decode by placing circles in that order, each at the sampled point of a fixed 60x60 grid that maximises its feasible radius given earlier circles (the radius is the min of wall distance and distance to placed circles minus their radii). Run a generational GA for a slice of the budget: tournament selection of size 3, uniform crossover of keys, Gaussian key mutation with sd 0.05, elitism of 2. Polish the best decoded packing with _solve_once using its centres and zero jitter, repair, and compare to the incumbent.

title: Island model with ring migration of elite packings
spec: Split the random-restart budget across 4 islands, each with its own rng drawn from seed plus island index and a local elite of size 3. Islands alternate in rounds: in each round each island performs 5 restarts (uniform random starts for the first two rounds, then starts from a random elite of its own or of the ring neighbour with probability 0.5 using the existing jitter). After every round, the best elite of each island is copied to the next island in the ring, replacing its worst elite if better. The global best is the incumbent that is returned. This is a batch-level change; the SLSQP solve and repair are unchanged.

title: Delaunay hole insertion after removing the smallest circle
spec: Once a guided restart is chosen from the incumbent, remove its smallest-radius circle. Build a Delaunay triangulation of the remaining centres plus four far-away corner ghost points using scipy.spatial.Delaunay. For each triangle, compute its circumcentre and the distance from the circumcentre to the nearest centre. Place the removed circle at the circumcentre with the largest such distance that lies inside [0, 1]^2. Then run the usual SLSQP solve from this configuration. The insertion uses the geometry of the largest empty triangle directly, rather than a random sample of hole locations.

title: Hard-disk NPT Monte Carlo compression
spec: Replace the SLSQP restart with a hard-disk Monte Carlo compression. Start from random non-overlapping centres in a box of side L=1 with small radii. Repeat sweeps: propose a random single-circle displacement and accept only if it creates no overlap and stays inside the box. Every sweep, also propose a volume move that scales all centres and L by a factor exp(eps), accepting with the NPT Metropolis rule at pressure P. Raise P geometrically across sweeps so the packing jams. Then set each circle's radius to half its nearest-neighbour or wall gap, and finish with the existing SLSQP polish from those centres. Use the seed rng for all moves and keep the best result by sum of radii.

title: Langevin dynamics on the overlap energy before SLSQP
spec: For each non-guided restart, start from uniform random centres and radii 0.05. Run 400 steps of overlap-energy Langevin dynamics: energy is the sum of squared positive overlaps of pairs, squared wall violations and a term -sum(r). Take an explicit gradient step with step size 1e-3 plus Gaussian noise of scale sqrt(2 T dt), where the temperature T decays geometrically from 0.05 to 1e-5 over the steps. Vectorise with numpy broadcasting. Use the final configuration as the SLSQP start, then run the existing _solve_once from it and repair.
